title: Sagan et al. v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC consolidated Case 2011-03 with the identical complaint in Case 2011-04 and denied both, holding that Covenant Presbytery did not err by receiving and acting on its MNA Committee’s report and recommendations concerning MJCCW.
first_summary: Ministers challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt and adoption of recommendations from its MNA Committee, alleging that the committee exceeded its assignment to investigate campus-minister salaries. The SJC denied the consolidated complaints. It held that examining Presbytery’s relationship with MJCCW naturally extended the salary inquiry, fell within the committee’s oversight responsibility, and produced recommendations for discussion rather than structural change. Presbytery had also ruled the matters properly before it and rejected an appeal from that ruling.
summary: Complainants challenged Covenant Presbytery’s receipt and adoption of recommendations from its MNA Committee, alleging that the committee exceeded its assignment to investigate campus-minister salaries. The SJC denied both consolidated complaints. It held that examining Presbytery’s relationship with MJCCW naturally extended the salary inquiry, fell within the committee’s oversight responsibility, and proposed discussion rather than structural change. Presbytery had also ruled the matters properly before it and rejected an appeal. The SJC could not independently verify assertions about the committee’s traditional oversight.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2011-03 is Paul Sagan et al. v. Covenant Presbytery; it was combined with Case 2011-04. The full SJC adopted the amended reasoning and opinion. Lines 11–15, 57–61, 97; printed pp. 554, 557, 559.
evidence_notes.dispute: The issue was whether Presbytery erred by receiving and acting on its MNA Committee’s report and recommendations concerning MJCCW. Lines 63–65; printed p. 557.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both complaints were denied. The inquiry naturally extended the salary assignment, the committee had MJCCW oversight, the recommendations proposed discussion rather than structural change, and Presbytery had upheld the moderator’s ruling. Lines 67–95; printed pp. 557–559.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC could not judge assertions about the traditional understanding of general oversight beyond collateral record evidence. Lines 93–95; printed p. 559.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the opinion itself supplies the judgment and reasons. Lines 67–97; printed pp. 557–559.
